resources.barrier_detail: PARTIAL BLOCK, twice. (1) First contact 2026-10-02T23:41:18Z: HTTP/2 429 from api.openalex.org (server: cloudflare), headers x-ratelimit-remaining: 0, x-ratelimit-remaining-usd: 0, retry-after: 1122; body {"error":"Rate limit exceeded","message":"Insufficient budget. This request has no API key, so it counts against the free daily budget shared by everyone on your network's IP address, and that budget is used up ($0 remaining; resets at midnight UTC)...","retryAfter":1122}. No API key was created (hard rule 4), so I polled every 45 s and logged 24 consecutive HTTP 429 probe responses between 23:41:18Z and 23:59:37Z. (2) At the 00:00 UTC budget reset the budget returned and 35 queries ran with HTTP 200 (20 stage-1 + 14 citation-chain + 1 stage-3). (3) The shared-IP budget was then exhausted again mid-stage-3: the 2nd stage-3 query returned HTTP 429 with retryAfter 84931 s (next midnight UTC), so 1 query returned no data and 6 further planned queries were never attempted. Net: 35/43 planned OpenAlex calls returned data.
resources.notes: No key, no account, no payment (hard rule 4 respected). Citation-chain expansion was the highest-yield move: cites:W2767260707 (Sewing 2017, 53 citing works), cites:W3126189506 (Slingsby 2022, 14 citing works) and the cited_by: reference lists of both anchors produced the strongest human-in-vitro leads. OpenAlex also resolved all three anchor records to primary IDs: Sewing 2017 = W2767260707 / PMID 29107969; Slingsby 2022 = W3126189506 / PMID 33567808 / DOI 10.3324/haematol.2020.260059; the control-ASO source paper = W7172412980 / PMID 42733805 / DOI 10.1016/j.omtn.2026.103051 (title: 'To scramble or not: Steric blocking 2'-MOE/PS control antisense oligonucleotides across cellular models'), which confirms the cASO7/cASO9/cASO11 Table S2 target exists and is indexed. Six still-unrun queries (morpholino/PMO x platelet, ex vivo donor x platelet, nusinersen lab parameters, iPSC/microphysiological x megakaryocyte, sequence-characterisation, recent-ASO-thrombocytopenia sweep) are listed verbatim above so a later run after the next UTC reset can execute them unchanged.

resources.barrier_detail: PARTIAL BLOCK by unauthenticated shared-pool rate limiting. Every call was retried up to 14 times with escalating backoff (4 s -> 25 s). Observed failure response, verbatim and repeatedly: HTTP/2 429, x-amzn-errortype: TooManyRequestsException, x-cache: Error from cloudfront, body {"message": "Too Many Requests. Please wait and try again or apply for a key for higher rate limits. https://www.semanticscholar.org/product/api#api-key-form", "code": "429"}. 126 individual HTTP 429 responses were logged in the first pass alone; successful calls needed between 1 and 14 attempts. Final tally: 35 of 42 calls returned HTTP 200. 7 calls never returned data after 14 attempts each: phosphorothioate+platelet+GPVI search (blocked on both the first pass and a dedicated retry pass), oblimersen+Bcl-2+thrombocytopenia search (blocked on both passes), the O'Brien CLL oblimersen phase III search, and the volanesorsen APPROACH platelet-count search. No API key was requested and no account created (hard rule 4).
resources.notes: Compensating coverage: the two queries permanently blocked here (phosphorothioate x platelet; oblimersen) were covered by the equivalent OpenAlex queries, which did return data, so the underlying evidence is not lost - but the Semantic Scholar rows for them are genuinely empty and are recorded as such. Semantic Scholar's unique contribution over OpenAlex was its /citations endpoint on 10.1089/nat.2022.0042 and PMID 32043907, which surfaced 10.1111/cts.13476 (BJAB in-vitro assay ranking vs clinical AEs) and 10.1016/j.omtn.2026.102976 (meta-analysis of AEs across ASO clinical studies), plus two 2025 AACR abstracts on ex vivo human whole-blood prediction of oligonucleotide immunotoxicity, and the complete aprinocarsen / ISIS 5132 / alicaforsen trial sets.
